passages.text: But someone will say, “If he has a form, he also has a shape and is in a place. If he is in a place and contained by it as something lesser, how is he great above all? And how can he be everywhere while having a shape?” To the person saying this, one can first say: those around Simon persuade people to believe such thoughts about him; but we know to be true the things attested by our Lord Jesus Christ. We are not obliged to provide you at a command with proofs that things are so. But first I will speak about place and God. Place is what does not exist, whereas God is what exists; and what does not exist cannot be compared with what exists. For how can place have existence, unless it is a second region, such as heaven, earth, water, air, or any other body, which would also fill the void there? It is called void for this reason: because it is nothing. Nothing is a more suitable name for it. For what is the so-called void—some sort of vessel that contains nothing? Yet the vessel itself, being empty, is not itself place; rather, if it is a vessel, place is that in which the empty vessel itself is. For what exists must necessarily be in what is nothing. This is what I mean by what does not exist, which some call place: it is nothing. How can what is nothing be compared with what exists, except as opposites, so that what exists is not called place, but what does not exist is? But even if it is something, although many examples press to come forth from me as proof, I wish to use just one, to show that what contains is not invariably stronger than what is contained. The sun is a circular shape and is wholly contained by air, but it illuminates the air, heats it, and cuts through it. When the sun is absent from it, the air is enveloped in darkness, and wherever a part of it becomes bright, it grows cold as though dying. But at the sun’s rising it is illuminated again, and wherever it is warmed by the sun it is also adorned with greater beauty. The sun does these things by its presence, although its substance is bounded. What, then, still prevents God, as the maker and master of this and all things, while he himself has shape, form, and beauty, from having the presence proceeding from him extended infinitely?

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἀληθεῖς γινώσκομεν τὰς μαρτυρουμένας
lexical_decisions.chosen: we know to be true the things attested
lexical_decisions.rationale: The feminine plural has no expressed noun; things or statements attested expresses the ellipsis without adding an extra source claim.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ μὲν ὂν μὴ ᾖ, τὸ δὲ μὴ ὂν τόπος λέγηται
lexical_decisions.chosen: what exists is not called place, but what does not exist is
lexical_decisions.rationale: Understands place from the second clause as the predicate to the first, not an assertion that what exists ceases to exist.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ οὗ ἂν αὐτοῦ μέρους λαμπρὸν γένηται, ὡς νεκρούμενον ψύχεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: wherever a part of it becomes bright, it grows cold as though dying
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied wording says bright, not dark. The resulting physical description is puzzling, but the main text preserves that printed adjective rather than silently emending it to fit the argument. Its referent is understood as a part of the air.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ μετουσίαν ἀπείρως ἐκτεταμένην ἔχειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: from having the presence proceeding from him extended infinitely
lexical_decisions.rationale: μετουσία can be presence, participation, or communicated influence. Presence preserves the analogy with the bounded sun’s effects without adding a second bodily substance.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὃ ἂν καὶ αὐτοῦ πληροῦν τὸ κενόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: which would also fill the void there
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes αὐτοῦ locatively, there, referring to the discussed place or region. It is not nominative emphatic αὐτό, itself. A genitive alternative is which would also fill its void, with the precise possessive referent drawn from the surrounding body/region discussion; no replacement Greek is adopted.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τί οὖν ἔτι κωλύει τὸν θεὸν ὡς τούτου καὶ πάντων δημιουργὸν καὶ δεσπότην ὄντα, αὐτὸν μὲν ἐν σχήματι καὶ μορφῇ καὶ κάλλει ὄντα, τὴν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ μετουσίαν ἀπείρως ἐκτεταμένην ἔχειν;
lexical_decisions.chosen: What, then, still prevents God, as the maker and master of this and all things, while he himself has shape, form, and beauty, from having the presence proceeding from him extended infinitely?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participial descriptions present God as maker/master and as himself being in shape, form, and beauty. The infinitive governed by prevents concerns his having the presence proceeding from him infinitely extended. The revised question preserves that grammatical focus rather than making the shape itself the prevented action and the extension merely circumstantial.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ οὗ ἂν αὐτοῦ μέρους λαμπρὸν γένηται, ὡς νεκρούμενον ψύχεται
source_issues.issue: The wording associates becoming bright with cooling, which is puzzling in this analogy. Bright is nevertheless what the supplied text says; no emendation to dark has been made.

passages.text: If, then, our Jesus also appeared to you through a vision, was made known, and conversed with you, it was as with an adversary, in anger. That is why he spoke through visions and dreams, or even through revelations that come from outside. But can anyone become wise for teaching through an apparition? If you say, “It is possible,” why did the teacher spend an entire year staying with people who were awake and conversing with them? And how shall we even believe you about the very claim that he appeared to you? How did he appear to you, when you think the opposite of his teaching? But if, after being seen and instructed by him for a single hour, you became an apostle, proclaim his words, explain his teachings, love his apostles, and do not fight me, who lived with him. For you have stood against me as an enemy, when I am a solid rock, a foundation of an assembly. If you were not an adversary, you would not, by slandering me, revile the proclamation that comes through me, so that I should not be believed when I say what I myself heard from the Lord while present—that is, as though I had been condemned and were unapproved. Or if you call me “condemned,” you accuse the God who revealed the Messiah to me and attack the one who pronounced me blessed on account of revelation. But if you truly wish to cooperate with the truth, first learn from us what we learned from him, and, becoming a disciple of truth, become our fellow worker.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπ’ ἐκείνου μιᾶς ὥρας ὀφθεὶς καὶ μαθητευθεὶς
lexical_decisions.chosen: after being seen and instructed by him for a single hour
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the passive being seen by him rather than silently reversing it into seeing him. The hour qualifies the short encounter and instruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: στερεὰν πέτραν ὄντα με, θεμέλιον ἐκκλησίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: when I am a solid rock, a foundation of an assembly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Peter’s self-description as rock/foundation. Church is a conventional alternative for ἐκκλησία, but the Greek does not specify a later institution.
Uses the POB title rendering because χριστός here functions independently, not in a personal-name construction.
Preserves the marked quoted verdict without identifying an unnamed opponent with a historical person not named in this section.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δηλονότι ὡς ἐμοῦ καταγνωσθέντος καὶ ἐμοῦ ἀδοκίμου ὄντος
lexical_decisions.chosen: —that is, as though I had been condemned and were unapproved
lexical_decisions.rationale: δηλονότι introduces an explanatory statement of the alleged grounds for withholding belief. That is preserves its scope outside the supposed condemnation rather than saying that condemnation itself was clear.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: διὰ τί ὅλῳ ἐνιαυτῷ ἐγρηγορόσιν παραμένων ὡμίλησεν ὁ διδάσκαλος;
lexical_decisions.chosen: why did the teacher spend an entire year staying with people who were awake and conversing with them?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The entire-year duration qualifies the teacher’s staying and conversing, not the duration of the listeners’ wakefulness. Spend an entire year expresses the temporal dative, staying represents παραμένων, and conversing preserves ὡμίλησεν. Awake remains the listeners’ state in contrast with a dream encounter, without a claim of uninterrupted yearlong wakefulness.
